transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for this afternoon's medication safety review of the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol, I'd like to hear from each of you on any operational findings before I sign off on the final decision. Pharmacy, let's start with you — any issues with stocking, labeling, or preparation in the automated dispensing cabinets? Laboratory medicine, are there any concerns about monitoring or turnaround times? Nursing education, how prepared do our nurses feel? And clinical IT, any flags from the electronic medication record ordering pathway? Please share whatever you've found so we can address it before the night shift.

transcript.text: Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. As a safeguard during a temporary hold, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes.

transcript.text: I have an important laboratory finding. The anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This is relevant to the safety review because it affects how we'll be monitoring patients receiving the intravenous anticoagulant, and nursing and clinical IT should be aware that aPTT ordering every six hours will be the lab pathway rather than anti-Xa levels.

transcript.text: I have a critical nursing education finding. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not yet completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. This is a significant safety concern that needs to be addressed before the protocol goes live on the night shift.

transcript.text: From a clinical IT perspective, I can confirm that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert can be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn prescribers about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This directly addresses the concentration selection errors Leah identified and adds an additional layer of safety before the protocol goes live on the night shift.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside automated dispensing cabinet stock of the intravenous anticoagulant; pharmacy to supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes until the medication safety review is complete and safeguards are in place.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Only the 1 mg/mL concentration will be dispensed via pharmacy-prepared syringes; the 2 mg/mL concentration will be removed from automated dispensing cabinets to prevent selection errors.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: aPTT testing every six hours will be the approved laboratory monitoring pathway until the anti-Xa analyzer is available for calibration on Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: All 18 nurses on tonight's shift who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering this medication.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn prescribers about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.

commitments.detail: Remove all bedside stock of the intravenous anticoagulant from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes until further notice.
Communicate to nursing and clinical IT that aPTT every six hours is the approved monitoring pathway until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated on Friday at 17:00.
Ensure all 18 uncertified nurses on tonight's shift receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering the anticoagulant; coordinate with the charge nurse to verify compliance before shift start.
Deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert in the electronic medication record at 16:00 today and confirm activation before the night shift begins.
